background_notes.fact: In the finite real product space Space, every compact set C is closed. Consequently Cᶜ×(a,b) is open in Space×ℝ for real a<b.

grounds.reason: Space carries its usual finite real product topology, which is Hausdorff.
F001 supplies compact C and the positive slab; its interval I is open.

background_notes.justification: For a point outside a compact set, separate it from each point of that set by disjoint neighborhoods and take a finite subcover on the compact set. Intersecting the corresponding finitely many neighborhoods of the outside point proves that the complement is open. Products of open sets are open in the product topology. This also holds for the zero-dimensional singleton space.

background_notes.fact: A constant map between the real normed spaces used in S002 is Fréchet differentiable with derivative the zero continuous linear map. Recursively, if X=Space×ℝ and Y=Value, the spaces Y_0=Y and Y_{ell+1}=L_cont(X,Y_ell) are real normed additive groups and real modules, so the same constant-derivative fact and M007 apply at every finite order.

grounds.reason: Space is a finite real normed vector space.
Value is a finite real normed vector space.
S002 repeatedly differentiates maps with domain Space×ℝ, first into Value and then into successive continuous-linear-map spaces, and compares each with a constant.

background_notes.justification: A constant map has identically zero increment, so its error after subtracting the zero linear map is zero and satisfies the derivative limit. Continuous linear maps carry the operator norm and pointwise real vector operations; the operator norm inequalities give a real normed vector space at each recursive stage. These facts supply only the zero-constant calculation and typing used by the displayed induction.

background_notes.fact: For a C² map g on an open neighborhood of p=(x,r) in Space×ℝ, put τ=(0,1), σ_j=(basis(j),0), and let π_k be component evaluation. Then the time derivative of π_k g(x,·) at r is π_k(Dg(p)τ), and the spatial j derivative of π_k g(·,r) at x is π_k(Dg(p)σ_j). With D²g(p)[v,w]=(D(Dg)(p)v)w, the second time derivative, second spatial j derivative and spatial j derivative of the time derivative are respectively π_k D²g(p)[τ,τ], π_k D²g(p)[σ_j,σ_j] and π_k D²g(p)[σ_j,τ]. Thus the fields V,A,Psp,Ssp,W in this packet are the corresponding evaluations of the first two spacetime derivatives.

Ssp differentiates Psp in the same spatial direction.

O is an open subset of U and the displayed induction proves vanishing of the first two spacetime derivatives there.

background_notes.justification: Time and spatial section maps are affine and have constant derivatives τ and the spatial embedding, respectively; π_k is continuous linear. Substituting their derivatives into the Fréchet chain rule gives the two first derivative formulas. Differentiating these formulas once more, with their directions fixed, gives the three second derivative formulas. Smoothness on the open U permits each local use. This verifies the section identification invoked in S002 without adding any regularity assumption or changing its induction route.

background_notes.fact: At every fixed r>0, each scalar component of a field continuous on U has a continuous section on all of Space. Finite products, finite sums, dot products and finite real linear combinations of these real sections are continuous. If the constituent sections vanish outside the same closed compact C, every displayed product, sum and linear combination also vanishes there, and each such h has compact tsupport contained in C.

grounds.reason: N001 gives smoothness, hence continuity, on U for all listed fields including e,d.
C is compact and I consists of positive times.
F002 gives all the needed vanishing on Cᶜ×I.
The family contains only the specified finite products, sums and real linear combinations.
A dot product is a finite sum of component products.
tsupport is the closure of the set where a function is nonzero.

background_notes.justification: For fixed positive r, x↦(x,r) is continuous with image in U; composing it and component evaluation with a continuous field proves section continuity. Continuous real addition and multiplication preserve continuity under each finite operation. Outside C all terms are zero, and finite homogeneous linear combinations remain zero. Thus support h⊆C; since C is closed, its closure tsupport h⊆C. The closure is closed, hence is a compact closed subset of the compact C.

background_notes.fact: The Borel product Lebesgue measure dx on Space=ℝ^(Fin n) has measurable open sets and is finite on every compact set, including n=0.

grounds.reason: Space has its Borel measurable structure and finite product topology.
dx is exactly the finite product of usual real Lebesgue measures.
These are the ambient measure hypotheses required for the actual M001 application.

background_notes.justification: Open sets are Borel. For any compact K, each continuous coordinate projection has compact, hence bounded, image in ℝ; boundedness follows by a finite subcover from the open intervals (-a,a). Since there are finitely many coordinates, K is contained in a box [-R,R]^(Fin n) for some finite R>0. This box has product Lebesgue measure (2R)^n<∞, so monotonicity bounds dx(K). For n=0 the empty product box is the entire singleton space and its product measure is the empty product 1. Thus the finite-on-compacts hypothesis holds without a positive dimension assumption.
